regions.text: 矛雇律と充足理由律とをライプニッツは「二大原理」と稱した（leibniz,Operaphiloopha-ca,edErdman,p515,goz）。矛盾律とは畢竟同一律にほかならない。「同一性の公理または同じことであるが矛盾の公理」（マm85）と云ってゐる。カントも雨者の區別をしなかつれ（Kant,Logak,hrsg¥Jishe,S5g）。

quote.translation: Leibniz called the law of contradiction and the law of sufficient reason the "two great principles" (Leibniz, Opera philosophica, ed. Erdmann, p. 515, 707), and for him the law of contradiction is in the end nothing other than the law of identity, as when he speaks of "the axiom of identity or, what is the same, the axiom of contradiction" (Ib., p. 136).

regions.text: 然らばこの二大原理たる「同一律」と「理由徘」とは如何なる踴係に立つか。

quote.translation: Kant, too, did not distinguish the two (Kant, Logik, hrsg. v. Jäsche, S. 58).

regions.text: ライプニッツは斷庁第一兵理」（Rrinaeveri-tates）において理由性を同一任へ還元せしめることの可能を示した。

quote.translation: In what relation, then, do these two great principles, the "law of identity" and the "law of ground", stand to each other?

regions.text: 述語は主語の内に歸結は前件の内に常に内在してるる（Semperpra

quote.translation: In the fragment "First Truths" (Primae veritates) Leibniz showed that groundedness can be reduced to identity.

quote.translation: The predicate or consequent is always inherent in the subject or antecedent (Semper praedicatum seu consequens inest subjecto seu antecedenti), and inherence (inesse) is nothing other than identity (idem esse), so that groundedness is, in the end, rooted in identity.
